quotes: Candidate 1 (combined score 0.807) edges candidate 2 (0.793) by 1.8%, within the 5% tiebreak band, so tiebreak criteria apply. Both candidates are identical in safety (1.000), geometry (1.000), and PVS (0.672); candidate 1 leads in chemistry (0.820 vs 0.760), kinetics (0.720 vs 0.680), and fluidics (0.820 vs 0.780), reflecting its slightly higher throughput and better alignment with the intensification screening objective. The researcher objective is a practical first flow experiment, not a demonstrated optimum; candidate 1 at Q=0.5 mL/min and τ=0.6 min is selected because its ±30% design envelope (Q: 0.35–0.65 mL/min, τ: 0.42–0.78 min) fully contains candidate 2's center point (Q=0.4 mL/min, τ=0.75 min), meaning a single run at candidate 1 conditions with a subsequent flow-rate screen naturally traverses both candidates' operating space. The most important remaining uncertainties are: (1) actual liquid holdup and true contact-time in the Cu/C CatCart packed bed — the 0.3 mL geometric volume is an upper bound on residence time, and bed voidage (unknown) will reduce effective τ; and (2) Cu leaching from the CatCart into the acetone product stream, which must be quantified by ICP-MS before any pharmaceutical application. The first bench experiment should verify that the system reaches steady state (confirmed by stable back-pressure and outlet concentration) within 3–5 reactor volumes (~1.5–2.5 min at 0.5 mL/min), then collect a sample for HPLC conversion analysis and ICP-MS Cu content; conversion and pressure drop are the primary go/no-go readouts. All conversion and productivity figures are unvalidated screening proxies derived from batch analogy kinetics and empty-tube hydraulic models that do not apply to this packed bed.

Allow an initial commissioning interval of at least 1.8 min, based on three nominal liquid-volume turnovers. Confirm steady outlet composition and stable flow, pressure and temperature before collection; elapsed time alone does not establish steady state. Measure phase holdup or tracer response when gas or a packed bed is present.

findings.classification: unsupported transport claims and dimensionally mixed explanation
quotes: CuAAC [3+2] cycloaddition of benzyl azide with phenylacetylene over heterogeneous Cu/C CatCart. Rate-limiting step is metalacycle formation at the Cu surface. Flow advantage: packed-bed provides continuous intimate substrate-catalyst contact, eliminating diffusion limitation present in batch. Acetone bp = 56 degC; at 150 degC operating temperature, vapour pressure ~11.3 bar, so 20 bar BPR (only available setpoint) is mandatory and sufficient. The 4 mm ID CatCart is larger than ideal for plug-flow (Pe ~4, significant axial dispersion per calculations); this is accepted as the only available reactor. Residence time is set to 0.6 min (0.3 mL / 0.5 mL/min) as a starting screen point; a residence time screen from 0.1 to 1.0 mL/min (0.3-3 min) is recommended. Benzyl azide must be handled dilute (0.25 M) and behind blast shield at all times. Cu leaching from CatCart into product stream is a known risk and should be monitored by ICP-MS. No deoxygenation required. No light source required or available.

Calculation: acetone vapour pressure at 150 degC ~11.3 bar. BPR required to maintain liquid phase. Only available BPR setpoint is 20 bar (bpr_xcube_20). 20 bar > 11.3 bar + 20 degC margin requirement. Analogy 1 used 8 bar BPR at 120 degC in DCM; our higher temperature and lower-bp solvent require higher BPR. 20 bar is the only available option and is sufficient.
findings.check: The qualitative claim that packed-bed contact eliminates diffusion limitation is not established by the supplied data. The pressure explanation adds a20 degree temperature margin to an11.3 bar vapor-pressure statement, which is dimensionally ambiguous. These are rationale weaknesses; this audit does not independently refute the selected20 bar operating point. The final procedure appropriately requests experimental checks rather than claiming measured conversion.

quotes: Reaction: heterogeneous N-benzhydryl hydrogenolysis of DMAOL over Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 (Pearlman's catalyst on alumina) under H2 at 21 bar/60°C in methanol. Mechanism: H2 dissociative chemisorption on Pd(0) → surface hydride → adsorption of DMAOL via benzhydryl C-N bond → hydride delivery cleaves C-N → 3-azetidinol + diphenylmethane desorb. Rate-limiting step is gas-liquid H2 mass transfer to catalyst surface. Batch gave only 38.1% conversion in 5 h at 21 bar, indicating severe mass-transfer limitation in stirred autoclave. Flow packed-bed provides 10–50× higher gas-liquid interfacial area (Taylor/trickle flow), expected to dramatically improve H2 delivery to Pd surface. Engineering calculations: τ = 20 min (IF = 15× vs batch), Q_liquid = 0.5 mL/min, V_reactor = 3.0 mL (inventory constraint — reactor_h2_pbr_300). Actual τ = 3.0 mL / 0.5 mL/min = 6.0 min liquid-phase residence time; this is shorter than the 20 min calculation target but is constrained by the fixed 3 mL inventory reactor. The 6 min flow residence time vs 300 min batch time represents a 50× intensification — consistent with mass-transfer-limited regime where flow advantage is large. BPR set to 21 bar (only available setpoint, matches batch pressure exactly). Analogies 1–3 are all dissimilar chemistry (Claisen rearrangement, photocatalytic C-N coupling) and provide no directly applicable hardware parameters; engineering calculations and Chemistry Plan are the primary basis. Particle size of Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 must be confirmed (target dp < 0.435 mm = ID/10 for 4.35 mm ID tube) before packing. Recommended_disposition: SCREEN — first experiment to establish conversion vs residence time baseline; catalyst lifetime and optimal gas:liquid ratio require experimental determination.
findings.check: The narrative attributes low batch conversion to severe mass-transfer limitation and asserts10–50-fold higher interfacial area in flow without supporting measurements. Batch conversion/time alone does not identify the rate-limiting mechanism. The final selection justification appropriately calls for measuring yield and performance; neither the correct arithmetic nor the cited nominal50-fold time ratio establishes experimental intensification.

Diagnostic only. At 3 bar BPR and 21°C, in-channel gas volume compressed ~3× relative to STP. Type II photosensitization: 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole absorbs at 420 nm, undergoes ISC to T1, sensitizes 3O2 to 1O2, which selectively oxidizes Fmoc-L-methionine thioether to sulfoxide. Key design decisions: (1) PFA tubing used (inventory constraint; PFA is transparent to visible light, compatible with MeCN, rated to 60°C and 10 bar). (2) 1 mm ID coil gives short optical path length for uniform photon delivery, addressing batch Beer-Lambert limitation. (3) Gas-liquid segmented flow with air MFC addresses O2 mass-transfer limitation (batch: headspace diffusion only). (4) BPR at 3.0 bar mandatory for gas-liquid system to maintain stable slug flow and prevent uncontrolled degassing. (5) Residence time set to ~4 min (inlet/STP basis) — longer than batch 5 min but justified by O2 transfer sufficiency warning (Da=92, O2 transfer 0.19× demand); screening at 2–8 min range recommended. (6) Analogies 1–3 are all single-phase photoredox (Ir/Ru, no gas co-feed) — not directly applicable for gas-liquid parameters; hardware parameters (FEP/PFA tubing, ~1–5 mL reactor, blue LED, 25–50°C) confirm general photochemistry flow setup. Residence time from analogies (12–30 min) is longer than our 5 min batch, so batch time is the primary anchor. (7) Over-oxidation to sulfone is a risk at long residence times — 4 min is conservative. (8) Incompatible pair: Fmoc + base — no base present, not a concern here.

interpretation_caution: Independent read-only content audit of all three corrected-schema-routing FlowPilot outputs. No judge grades were read or changed; no scores are assigned here. Checks concern delivered design content and explicit arithmetic, not measured conversion, safety certification or exhaustive chemical validation. Comparison with the original six-output audit isolates a harness format confound; all archived primary outcomes remain unchanged.
